content: 1. Logging in is not mandatory for viewing or editing pages, but it offers additional features and is generally recommended. 2. To create a user account, you must provide a username (either your real name or a nickname) and a password. Usernames already in use will be rejected. 3. Once an account is created, it is permanent, and you are considered logged in. For subsequent logins, you must provide the same username and password to verify your identity. 4. Edits made while logged in are attributed to your username, whereas edits made without logging in are recorded under your IP address. 5. Some MediaWiki projects allow a single login across multiple related projects, such as the Wikia family of over 1,000 projects. However, on Wikimedia projects, logging in and setting preferences must currently be done separately for each wiki. 6. If you are not logged in, you can view your IP address by checking the page history. Benefits of Logging In: 7. Logging in allows other users to recognize you by your username, which is more consistent and less cumbersome than an IP address, especially if you use different devices or locations. 8. You gain access to a personal user page where you can share information about yourself and a user talk page for communication with other users. 9. Logged-in users can mark edits as minor, reducing inconvenience for others. 10. You can track changes to pages of interest using a watchlist. 11. If you provide an email address, other users can contact you anonymously via email without knowing your actual email address. 12. You can rename pages and customize your preferences, such as the number of pages displayed in Recent changes or the site's appearance using different skins. How to Log In: 13. Configure your browser to accept cookies from the specific wiki you plan to edit. 14. Click the Log in link at the top right of the page and enter your username and password. If you are a new user, follow the link to create an account. 15. You may optionally provide an email address for anonymous communication. 16. Selecting the Remember me option will save your login credentials on the same computer, eliminating the need to re-enter your password. However, this feature does not work with passwords generated by MediaWiki software, so it is recommended to change your password. 17. Logging in and setting preferences must be done separately for each wiki, but you can maintain a consistent username across multiple wikis if the name is available. Troubleshooting Login Issues: 18. Usernames and passwords are case-sensitive. The first character of the username is capitalized by default. 19. If you registered on a different version of Wikipedia (e.g., Spanish Wikipedia or Wikibooks), you must create a new username for the current version. 20. If you appear logged out immediately after logging in, it is likely a cookie issue. Some firewall or ad-blocking software may also interfere with cookies. 21. If you are automatically logged out after logging in, your ISP may be using transparent proxies. In such cases, try using a secure server to bypass the proxy. This issue is common with certain satellite ISPs. 22. Occasionally, users may be logged out unexpectedly due to browser settings, cache, or server glitches during high server loads. Selecting the Remember me option can help mitigate this issue. Password Recovery: 23. If you forget your password and have provided an email address, you can request a temporary password by entering your username on the login screen and clicking E-mail new password. 24. If no email address was provided or the address is outdated, you will need to create a new account. Creating an Account: 25. To create an account, click Log in at the top right of the page and select Create an account. Provide a username, password, and complete a CAPTCHA test to verify you are human. 26. If you cannot view the CAPTCHA due to accessibility issues, you can request account creation assistance at Wikipedia:Request an account. 27. Since September 26, 2006, usernames containing the @ symbol are not permitted. Setting Preferences: 28. Click the Preferences link at the top right of the page to access options such as changing your password or customizing the site's appearance using different skins. User Page and Talk Page: 29. Logged-in users can create a personal user page to share information about themselves and their interests. 30. You also have a user talk page where others can leave messages, and you can respond. These pages can be edited like any other MediaWiki page. Logging Out: 31. To log out, click the Log out link at the top right of the page. Username Impersonation: 32. In some sans-serif fonts, the capital letter I and the lowercase letter l may appear identical. If your username contains one of these characters, consider creating a secondary account with swapped letters to prevent impersonation. Redirect the dummy account's user page to your real account. 33. Since the implementation of bugzilla:2290, accounts similar to existing ones can only be created by administrators. If you cannot create a similar account, others cannot either, reducing the risk of impersonation.
